newsitem.title: UK: Deloitte & Touche says higher UK VAT rate possible.
newsitem.headline: Deloitte & Touche says higher UK VAT rate possible.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government looks increasingly likely to raise the general rate of value-added tax (VAT) in its first budget on July 2, possibly to 20 percent, accountants Deloitte & Touche said.

It said that although Labour had ruled out extending VAT to zero-rated goods such as books, magazines and children's clothes, it had not ruled out an increase in the general rate, presently 17.5 percent, to perhaps 20 percent.
"This measure could raise as much as five billion pounds in additional revenue," Deloitte & Touche said.

Its views were at odds with those of tax firm KPMG, which said on Tuesday it thought hefty increases in either VAT or income tax were unlikely, given Labour's criticism of Conservative VAT increases and its commitments not to raise income tax rates.

Deloitte & Touche noted that standard VAT rates in the European Union ranged from 15 percent in Ireland to 25 percent in Denmark and said there was pressure for the lower VAT rates to rise in preparation for harmonisation in the EU.

"If the new government needs to raise significant amounts of revenue -- in addition to that to be raised by the windfall tax -- then VAT would appear to be the obvious choice and now would be the most propitious time to do it," the company's VAT partner Tony McClenaghan said.
